source.title: The Answer-Basin Representation Hypothesis: We Are Not Probing or Steering Concepts
source.authors: Man-Jiang Yu; Hongji Li; Zi-Han Wang; Jun-Wei Chen; Xue Li; Priyanka Singh; Yang Cao; Li-Jie Hu

page_placements.theme: Measurement sensitivity, identifiability and canonical feature identities

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies answer-basin statistics and their relation to behavior-level linear probes and steering vectors. It does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity-limited polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, or whether represented features are one-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about answer-basin representation geometry and steering, which are related to linear representations but do not measure the superposition claims in V1–V6. Rows below are recorded as findings about this related construct. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper studies whether behavior-level probe and steering directions (correctness, bias, safety) track the model's answer-probability measure. It never mentions superposition, polysemantic neurons, sparse features, SAEs or feature dimensionality, and has no result bearing on V1–V6. It neither tests nor uses superposition, so T6; 'cites_only' is the closest relation, though the paper does not even cite Toy Models of Superposition. The reader's 'discusses' overstates the link: superposition is never discussed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the model's answer measure organizes behavior-level probe and steering directions. Probing and steering behave as the concept intends under label–mass alignment, weaken as mass gaps shrink, and reverse under conflict. Nothing is concluded about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and tests an answer-basin representation account; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported representation and steering effects vary with source and target answer-mass relations; the paper also uses different residual-stream blocks for BBQ and SafetyBench steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct and wrong answer representations separate more in PCA as the answer-mass gap grows; their distributions overlap more as it shrinks (Qwen2.5-7B, Fig. 1; other models in Figs. 9–11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Answer-basin mass gaps are associated with the geometry of behavior-level answer representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Reversing source label–mass alignment yields nearly opposite projected steering vectors. Out-of-fold signed projections correlate with log-mass contrast (r=0.770 BBQ, r=0.802 SafetyBench).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Answer-mass relations in source data shape the orientation of behavior-level steering directions.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed correct-minus-wrong vector favors the correct answer under alignment and the wrong answer under conflict (Gemma-3-4B-PT, BBQ and SafetyBench).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The target question's answer-mass ordering determines which answer a fixed label-defined steering vector favors.

fits_no_version.finding: Probes trained under Align beat the mean-logp baseline and Conflict-trained probes fall below it in all 12 model–dataset combinations. Probes trained on wrong-only pairs still recover mass ordering (Fig. 3, Tables 2 and 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavior-level correctness probes read out answer-mass ordering rather than the labeled concept.

record.problems: The paper notes finite-sample error and uncertainty in grouping free-form responses; many experiments therefore use candidate-answer measures over fixed answer spaces. The displayed steering and PCA geometry includes figure-based results, and the reported experiments do not address sparse-feature superposition.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1–4 and Figure 12 report answer-concentration or answer-mass probe performance and correctness-selection metrics; they were not extracted because they do not measure the claim versions' feature overlap, capacity pressure, SAE features, or feature dimensionality.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity or feature-count manipulation, no feature geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons, no dictionary or SAE recovery; linear probes on behavior labels are not feature-recovery tests.
All: single linear probe and steering directions are assumed, not tested against multi-dimensional alternatives.

record.verdict_notes: All 15 rows correctly carry versions ['none']; their states and values match the text and figures. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because the paper never addresses superposition. Probe-performance results (Tables 1–4, Figs. 3 and 12) were left out of the rows; they are irrelevant to V1–V6 and are noted only in fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features exceeding network dimensions, feature overlap and orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemantic neurons, including dedicated dimensions for important features and sharing by others.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Feature distribution across neurons and recovery of sparse features with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.operation_detail: Compared correct- and wrong-answer representations across candidate answer-basin mass gaps using a shared PCA space.
rows.measure: PCA separation of correct- and wrong-answer representations
rows.value: Text reports clearer separation for larger gaps and increasing overlap as gaps shrink.
rows.note: This is answer-basin representation geometry, not a test of feature superposition.

relation.reason: The text does not cite superposition as a finding. It discusses related linear-representation and circuit research; discusses is the closest available relation for this adjacent conceptual treatment.

tranche.reason: The study tests an answer-measure account of probing and steering, without testing or using superposition or any of V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Observed states describe answer-basin effects only; the rows' none version links and empty verdict list are appropriate.
